Dev.releaseNotes:
`fix` (`tmdb`): **Drop the memoised titles and overviews when they are written**:

The TMDB entities memoise their titles and overviews on first read, but the
rows themselves belong to `TMDB_Title` and `TMDB_Overview`, which are served by
direct repositories. Writing to those said nothing to the entity holding the
memoised copy, and the entities come from cached repositories that outlive any
one request, so a title corrected on TMDB stayed stale for the life of the
process — a forced refresh reported no change, and only a restart brought the
new value through.

`AnimeSeries` compounded it. `ResetAnimeTitles` and `ResetPreferredOverview`
run right after a TMDB refresh and rebuild by reading back through the entity,
so they re-cached the stale values as fresh. `ResetPreferredTitle` never
cleared anything at all: its guard returned early precisely when a title was
cached, making every one of its call sites a no-op.

- Added `ResetAllTitles` and `ResetAllOverviews` to `IEntityMetadata`, with
  default empty bodies so an entity overrides only what it actually memoises,
  and implemented them on `TMDB_Movie`, `TMDB_Show`, `TMDB_Season`,
  `TMDB_Episode`, `TMDB_Collection` and `TMDB_Person`
- Dropped the memoised copies in `UpdateTitlesAndOverviewsWithTuple` as soon as
  the rows are saved, so the series-level resets that follow rebuild from the
  new values rather than the old ones
- Fixed `ResetPreferredTitle` to clear unconditionally, matching
  `ResetPreferredOverview` and `AniDB_Anime.ResetPreferredTitle`. It stays
  eager because `AnimeSeriesRepository.RegenerateDb` uses it to warm the cache
  on startup

The purge paths need no invalidation of their own: they delete the entity from
its cached repository, so the memoised copy goes with it.

Closes #1422

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Store the biographies fetched for a staff member**:

`UpdatePerson` asked TMDB for `PersonMethods.Translations` and then only ran
`Populate`, which keeps the English biography and drops the rest. Nothing else
wrote a `TMDB_Overview` row for a person, so `GetAllBiographies` always came
back empty and `GetPreferredBiography` always fell through to the English
fallback, whatever the preferred description languages were set to.

- Reconciled the biographies from the translations already on hand, so they are
  stored the way every other entity's overviews are
- Added an `includeTitles` flag to `UpdateTitlesAndOverviews`, passed as
  `false` here. A person has no titles to speak of — you would not translate a
  given name or a family name — so TMDB carries none and `TMDB_Person` has
  nothing to read them back with; without the flag the English name would be
  written as a title row that nothing ever reads
- Purged the biographies in `PurgePersonInternal`, which removed the person,
  their images and their cast and crew roles but left their overviews behind.
  That was harmless while nothing wrote them and an orphaned row once
  something did

`refactor` (`anidb`): **Skip MyList sync steps that would write nothing**:

A sync planned and queued a removal for every entry the library no longer
had, without checking whether the entry was already at the state the delete
type marks with. Under `MarkDeleted` such an entry stays in the MyList and
keeps reading as missing, so every sync re-queued the same no-op edit against
it — thousands per run on a large list, each one taking a turn in the
`AniDB_UDP` concurrency group ahead of real work. The same hole existed on the
watched path, where a decided update that `IsInDesiredState` disagreed with
was enqueued anyway.

- Skipped the enqueue in `SyncInternalAsync` when the entry already holds the
  marked state, on both the file and the generic episode paths, and did the
  same in `ReconcileEntry`
- Renamed `MylistSyncActionKind.AlreadyInDesiredState` to `NoOperation`, which
  no longer implies a fault; the decision-versus-desired-state disagreement it
  used to stand for is now a warning in the log
- Added `MylistSyncOptions.IncludeNoOperations`, off by default, so a plan can
  list what a sync looked at and left alone as well as what it will do. Like
  `PlanOnly` it describes the call rather than the server, so no setting backs
  it
- Collected the plan through a `MylistSyncActionLog`, so what a no-op means for
  the plan is decided once rather than at each of the dozen sites that record
  one
- Added `EntriesAlreadyDisposed`, `EpisodesAlreadyDisposed` and `NoOperations`
  to `MylistSyncResult`, and a left-alone count to the sync summary log, so the
  removal counts dropping to zero is explained rather than just observed
- Dropped the empty-`Hash` filter in `AddMissingFiles`; a `VideoLocal` always
  has one

Closes #1419

`fix` (`relocation`): **Report moved/renamed flags correctly when move or rename is disabled**:

ConvertToResponse passed the filename and directory comparisons to
RelocationResponse.FromResult in swapped slots, and computed them
against the renamer's proposed name/path even when move or rename
was disabled. With move=false and rename=false, the relocation
preview endpoints therefore reported IsRelocated=true.

- Passed the directory comparison as moved and the filename
  comparison as renamed, matching the FromResult signature
- Gated both flags on shouldMove/shouldRename and the SkipMove/
  SkipRename result flags so they stay false when the effective
  destination is the file's current location

`fix` (`search`): **Match titles when the query carries a trailing qualifier** ([#1411](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1411)):

`MinEditDistInText` is semi-global over the text only — row 0 is all
zeros for a free text-prefix skip, and the result is the minimum over
the last row for a free text-suffix skip. Slop in the *query* was
charged in full, so a query carrying a token the title lacks, such as
`Sousou no Frieren (2023)` against a stored `Sousou no Frieren`, scored
5 edits and blew past the cap of 3 in `GetMaxErrors`. The length gate
`normalized.Length >= normalizedQuery.Length - maxErrors` skipped the
comparison outright before a distance was even computed.

Adding a year is always exactly 5 edits regardless of query length, so
neither raising the cap nor relaxing the gate alone was enough. The
parentheses were never the problem — `NormalizeForIndex` already maps
`(`, `)`, `[` and `]` to spaces, so `[2023]` and a bare `2023` failed
identically. The cliff was not year-specific either: `S1` and `(TV)`
squeaked through at exactly `dist == maxErrors`, while anything four or
more characters longer fell off.

`TryGetFuzzyDistance` replaces the gate and the direct distance call in
both `FuzzySearchIndex.SearchLatin` and `SeriesSearch.SearchCollection`.
When the query is longer than the title it swaps the arguments, moving
the free prefix/suffix onto the query, and guards the swapped path with
`title.Length * 2 >= query.Length` so a two-letter title like `GK`
cannot match nearly every query. The guard applies only to the swapped
direction, leaving a short typo'd query matching a long title as before.

Prior to `dc486893c` the Sorensen-Dice path tolerated all of these; it
compared bigram sets, so five unmatched characters out of twenty-two
barely moved the score.

- Added `TryGetFuzzyDistance` covering both directions and both guard
  rejections
- Added end-to-end cases for `(2004)`, `[2024]`, a bare year, `(TV)`,
  and a typo stacked on a trailing year
- Added cases pinning the mirror direction, the `ExactMatch` flag
  staying false for slop matches, strict mode staying strict, and short
  titles not matching much longer queries

`perf` (`anidb`): **Compress both MyList caches with Brotli, and store the generic index as gaps**:

`generics.json` sat uncompressed at 2.2 MB, making it the largest file in the
MyList directory — larger than the whole compressed MyList cache beside it.
Neither file is read by eye and both run to hundreds of thousands of entries.

Measured on a real index of 294,947 generic IDs and a MyList cache of 34,016
entries:

- `generics.json` 2,230,718 bytes -> `generics.json.br` around 87,000
- `mylist.json.gz` 1,305,346 bytes -> `mylist.json.br` 1,206,892

The generic index also stores the sorted IDs as the gap from one to the next
rather than in full. They cluster hard — 80% of the gaps are exactly 1 — so
most of the file becomes a run of ones that compresses to almost nothing, which
is worth more than compression alone.

The two caches are written at different levels because they are written at
different rates, and the level is not a free choice:

- The MyList cache is flushed every five seconds, so it uses quality 4. That is
  both smaller and slightly faster than the gzip it replaces, while quality 11
  takes twenty-two seconds a write and would never finish before the next flush
- The generic index is fetched once a day, so it uses quality 11 and can afford
  the second it costs

Neither file left behind is cleaned up. Both have only been on disk for hours,
and the next sync fetches a fresh copy regardless, so tidying them is not worth
the code. That is why the pre-refactor backup is treated differently: it has
been accumulating on every install since long before either cache existed.

- Moved the shared read and write into `CompressedJsonFile`, so the two caches stop keeping their own copies of it
- `Persist_IsDebouncedUntilFlushed` named the cache file directly and would have passed against a missing one, since `GetLastWriteTimeUtc` returns the same sentinel for both sides of that comparison

`fix` (`anidb`): **File the legacy MyList backup instead of deleting it**:

Removing `mylist.json` reclaimed the disk but threw away a backup. It holds the
only record of what a user's MyList looked like when it was taken, and older
builds wrote it and never rotated it, so for some installs it is the oldest one
they have.

It is now compressed and moved into `Backups/` alongside the rest. Nothing ever
recorded when it was taken, so its own modified time names it, which also puts
it in the right place once the backups are sorted.

It is still never read. The entries predate fields the sync compares on, so it
is copied across as bytes rather than parsed, and `legacy` goes in the name so
anyone restoring from it knows the shape is older. Beyond that it is an
ordinary backup — the name matches the rotation pattern, so it ages out with
the others rather than sitting there forever.

- Moved the backup directory and naming into `MylistBackups`, so the rotation pattern and the filename format stop being restated in two places

`feat` (`api`): **Accept `includeDataFrom` on the `/api/v3/Series` list endpoints**:

Most of the `/api/v3/Series/*` endpoints already take `includeDataFrom`, but
the list endpoints did not, so populating the `AniDB` property of a listed
series meant a second call to `/api/v3/Series/AniDB` for every row.

The parameter is bound and passed through exactly as it is on
`/api/v3/Series/{seriesID}`, and the `Series` model already reads it, so
nothing changes for a caller that omits it.

Applied to `/api/v3/Series/WithManuallyLinkedFiles` as well as the two the
issue named. It is the sibling of `WithoutFiles` — same shape, same file — and
supporting the parameter on two of the three list endpoints would have been an
odd seam to leave behind.

Closes #1415

`fix` (`anidb`): **Stop loading the legacy MyList backup as a cache**:

`mylist.json` is the backup older builds wrote before backups moved into
`Backups/` and gained rotation. It was only ever written, never read back, and
its entries predate fields the sync now compares on — so reading it seeded the
cache with entries that looked complete and were not.

It is now deleted on load instead. The cache starts empty, `LastFetchedAt`
stays null, and the freshness check fails, so the next sync fetches a fresh
copy rather than reconciling against a half-populated one.

The bare-array format went with it. That shape was only ever reachable through
this file, as the compressed cache has carried the `CacheFile` wrapper and its
fetch stamp since the day it was introduced.

- Gave the delete its own error handling, so failing to remove a file we refuse to read cannot stop the compressed cache from loading
- Dropped the matching cleanup in `Persist`, leaving one place that removes it
- Renamed `LegacyCachePath` to `LegacyBackupPath`, since it was never a cache
- Replaced the migration test with one pinning the new contract: the entry is not loaded, the file is gone, and nothing is marked as fetched

`refactor` (`anidb`): **Rework MyList into a plugin-facing service with a local cache**:

AniDB MyList had no plugin-facing surface at all, and every operation went
straight out over UDP. Reading a single entry's state meant a round trip, an
edit meant a second round trip to read back what had just been written, and
nothing local remembered what AniDB was holding.

**Added `IMyListService`** to `Shoko.Abstractions`, with the models and enums
it needs — `MyListEntry`, `MyListAddData`, `MyListUpdateData`,
`MyListSyncOptions`, `MyListSyncResult`, and `MyListState`,
`MyListFileState`, `MyListReadStates`,
`MyListDeleteType`, `MyListFetchMode`, `MyListWatchedSyncMode`. Entry-level
and video-level operations both live here; the video-level ones resolve their
defaults and then delegate to the entry-level ones rather than duplicating
them.

**Added a local cache** behind the service, indexed by list ID, file ID, ED2K
and episode ID, so a lookup does not go out to AniDB. It refreshes when stale
on the same terms as the HTTP MyList export, rather than on a schedule, and
writes back through a debounced flush instead of rewriting the whole file on
every change. It is stored gzipped, migrating an existing `mylist.json` in
place on first load.

**Identified generic entries from the supplementary generics index** rather
than inferring them from the file state, which was never a reliable marker.
`MyListEntry.IsGeneric` is a tri-state, so an entry whose kind could not be
resolved is left alone rather than being disposed of on a guess. The index is
opt-in.

Also in this change:

- `MyListFetchMode` replaces the old force flag, so a caller can ask for
  cache-only, cache-then-network or network-only. `IgnoreTimeCheck` is a
  modifier rather than a transport, so it composes with whichever
  transports are configured instead of replacing them
- An edit patches the cached entry from the values it just sent instead of
  re-fetching, removing the second UDP round trip
- Remove-vs-mark is decided at the caller rather than inside the job
- A generic entry is kept while another manually linked release still
  relies on it, instead of being disposed of along with the first one
- Colliding syncs merge through `IJobMerge` instead of the later one being
  dropped, and the recurring sync is registered through the service so a
  frequency change keeps its configurator
- Added the Blu-ray file state, and stopped sending any file state the UDP
  API would reject — the API validates a `filestate` write more narrowly than
  it reports one
- Watched dates are held at the precision AniDB can carry, which is a date
  with no time
- Dropped `VideoLocal.MyListID`; the cache is the source of truth now
- Stubbed out the v1 `AniDB/MyList/Missing` endpoints and dropped
  `CL_MissingFile`; they pulled the full MyList export over HTTP on every
  call and never fed it back into any cache
- Dropped the sync's own schedule gate, which re-derived the recurring
  interval a second time from a `ScheduledUpdate` row. The recurring
  registry already owns that interval, and the gate never opened at all
  once the frequency was `Never` — the default — so an explicitly
  requested sync could be swallowed. The v2 `anidb/list/sync` endpoint
  now forces, matching its v1 and v3 counterparts
- `SyncAsync` runs one sync at a time. It is on the plugin contract, so it
  can be called without the queue job that would otherwise serialise it;
  a call made while a sync is running returns `null` rather than starting
  a second one. Otherwise it returns a `MyListSyncResult` with the counts
  the sync had only been logging
- Fixed the UDP debug endpoint reporting a 505 as a login failure

`feat` (`anidb`): **Add MyList actions at group, series, episode and file level**:

The MyList had one scoped entry point, `POST /File/{fileID}/AddToMyList`,
and no way to act on a whole group, series or episode. The `Video` and
`Episode` action scopes had base classes but no implementations at all, so
these are the first of either.

Added `AddToMyList` and `RemoveFromMyList` at all four scopes. Every scope
above a video fans out to the files beneath it, because a MyList entry is
per file. The removals ask for confirmation, since they change state on
AniDB rather than locally.

There is no separate update action: `ScheduleAddVideo` already answers
`FILE_ALREADY_IN_MYLIST` by editing the entry, so adding is how an existing
entry gets its state refreshed.

Also in this change:

- Added `IMyListService.ScheduleDisposeVideo`, so the rule for how a video
  maps onto MyList entries — its own entry for an AniDB release, the generic
  entry of each linked episode for a manual link — lives in one place. The
  four removal actions and `VideoService.ScheduleRemovalFromMyList` all go
  through it instead of restating it
- `VideoService.ScheduleRemovalFromMyList` picks up the shared-generic-entry
  guard it never had, so removing one manually linked file no longer takes
  the MyList coverage of another file on the same episode with it

`feat` (`anidb`): **Add a video-scoped MyList sync and `Sync MyList` actions**:

Syncing was all-or-nothing: the only way to reconcile one series' entries was
to sync the whole MyList. Added `SyncAsync` and `ScheduleSync` overloads
taking an `IEnumerable<IVideo>` ahead of the arguments the unscoped pair
already took, and a `Sync MyList` action at group, series, episode and file
level on top of them. There is no single-video method; one video is a
one-element enumerable.

A scoped sync adds what is missing and reconciles watched and storage states,
but never removes. An entry is only removed when its local file is gone, which
cannot be true of a video the caller handed in, so removing would mean acting
on entries outside the scope.

Rather than a second implementation, `SyncInternalAsync` took an optional
scope. A file entry is covered when it maps to one of the videos, and a
generic entry when it maps to an episode one of them is linked to, since that
is the only entry AniDB holds for a manual link.

Also in this change:

- Added `SyncAniDBMyListVideosJob`, keyed on a hash of its video set so two
  syncs over different sets stay separate jobs while two over the same set
  collide and merge. It shares the AniDB HTTP concurrency group with
  `SyncAniDBMyListJob`, so a scoped sync and a full one never run at once and
  neither has to skip
- Reordered the sync loop to resolve the episode and video once up front,
  dropping a duplicate `GetByReleaseURI` and `GetByEd2k` per entry

`feat` (`anidb`): **Sync generic MyList entries against episodes without files**:

Watched state only ever flowed one way for an episode with no file. The sync
loop is driven by the entries AniDB returns, so it could reconcile a generic
entry it already knew about but never create one, and `AddMissingFiles` walks
local videos only. An episode watched locally with no file — or held only
through a manual link, which has no file entry of its own — was invisible to
the sync entirely, and `ScheduleAddAllManualLinks` was the only thing that
ever created an entry for the latter.

Added `AddMissingEpisodes`, a local-driven sweep that runs alongside the
remote-driven loop. An episode whose local videos all lack an AniDB file entry
is one the file tier cannot own, so:

- held by a manual link — create the generic entry that covers it, whether or
  not it has been watched
- no local videos at all — record the watch through the new
  `MyListWatchedEpisodeMode`: leave it alone, attach it to the oldest entry
  AniDB already holds, or add a generic entry. `AttachToOldest` picks the
  lowest list ID, falling back to the lowest file ID, and creates a generic
  when there is nothing to attach to

A generic entry recording nothing at all — no local file, no local watch and
nothing watched upstream either — is removed instead, since the only reason
one exists is to record a watch for a file the user does not have.

**Added `MyListSyncTargets`** so a sync can be asked for the file tier, the
episode tier or both. It is a flag set on `MyListSyncOptions`, backed by
`MyList_SyncTargets`, and defaults to reconciling both.

**Added episode-scoped syncing** — `SyncAsync` and `ScheduleSync` overloads
taking an `IEnumerable<IShokoEpisode>`, and `SyncAniDBMyListEpisodesJob` to
carry them. A scope now holds both sets whichever way it was built, so an
episode scope drags in the videos linked to it and one call reconciles the
episode's generic entry alongside the file entries of any files it has. The
episode-level `Sync MyList` action goes through it, so it now works for an
episode with no files at all.

Also in this change:

- Both new options are nullable on `MyListSyncOptions` and resolved from
  settings like the other nine, and both are flattened onto all three sync
  jobs so an explicitly requested value survives being enqueued
- The sweep respects `MyList_AddFiles`, and the removal respects
  `DeleteLocalOnly`, so neither acts against a user who asked Shoko to leave
  their MyList alone

`refactor` (`anidb`): **Extract the MyList watched-state rules from the two copies of them**:

`ProcessStates` and `ProcessGenericEntry` were a pair of ~130-line near-clones.
Both carried the same same-day-clash cascade, the same read/set fallbacks and
the same terminal state check, and both had their effects wired into every
branch of it, so the rules could only be read by tracing five call sites and
could not be tested at all.

Pulled the rules out as `MyListSyncDecisions.DecideWatchedAction`, a pure
function of the two dates, the entry's update day and the sync settings,
answering with an import, an export or nothing. Reconciling an entry is then
one `ReconcileEntry` that applies the answer, parameterised by the three things
that actually differ between a file entry and a generic one: where the local
date comes from, how an import is written back, and how the entry is
identified.

`MyListService` is 139 lines shorter for it, and the rules now live in one
place instead of two that had to be kept in step by hand.

Also in this change:

- Added `MyListSyncDecisionEquivalenceTests`, which keeps a transcription of
  the branch chain the rules were extracted from and diffs the two across
  every combination of both dates, a same-day and an older update, all
  sixteen read/set combinations and all three sync modes — 1920 cases. It is
  expected to fail if the rules are ever changed on purpose, so both sides
  get updated together
- Added `MyListSyncDecisionTests` covering the rules directly, the first
  tests of any kind over the reconciliation

`feat` (`anidb`): **Let a MyList sync report what it did, or preview what it would do**:

A sync reported counts and nothing else, so there was no way to see what it was
about to change before it changed it, and no way for a plugin to inspect what a
run had done.

**Added `MyListSyncAction`** to `Shoko.Abstractions`, one step of a sync: what
kind it is, a line describing it, the identity of whatever it acts on, and the
watched state, storage state or delete type it carries. `MyListSyncResult` now
returns every step in the order it took them.

The kinds are named for the direction they move data in — `ImportWatchedState`
is the only one that writes locally, while `ExportWatchedState`,
`ExportEntryAddition` and `ExportEntryRemoval` write the MyList. Reading that
off the name is for people; `MyListSyncAction.Direction` is for code, and it
classifies every kind explicitly rather than defaulting, so a kind added later
cannot quietly inherit the wrong side.

**Added `MyListSyncOptions.Preview`**, which works the plan out and returns it
without doing any of it. The MyList itself is still fetched, since the plan is
derived from it, but nothing local is written and nothing is sent to AniDB.
Every effect the sync has is behind the flag: both imports, the entry updates,
both sweeps and both removal drains.

Also in this change:

- `Preview` is read from the caller's options rather than the resolved ones. It
  is not settings-backed, so resolving it would have dropped it and the flag
  would have silently done nothing

`refactor`: **Spell Mylist as one word, and gather it under one namespace**:

`MyList` was spelled as two words throughout — types, members, namespaces and
filenames alike. As an identifier it is one word, the same way AniDB is `Anidb`
and TMDb is `Tmdb`.

Renamed `MyList` to `Mylist` and `myList` to `mylist` across the identifiers,
and moved `MylistService`, `MylistCache` and `MylistGenericsCache` into a new
`Shoko.Server.Services.Mylist` namespace alongside the reconciliation rules,
which were also split out of `MylistSyncDecisions.cs` so each type has its own
file.

The two spellings differ only in the case of one letter, so the HTTP API is
unaffected either way: route matching and incoming JSON properties are both
case-insensitive, and a client calling `SyncMyList` still reaches
`SyncMylist`.

Three things keep the two-word spelling:

- Prose, so doc comments still read "the MyList" while an identifier they
  reference — `MylistEntry`, `MylistFetchMode` — does not
- The user data directory, so an existing `MyList/` folder is still found and
  its cache is not silently orphaned and refetched
- The `MyList_` settings, which are internal rather than plugin-facing. The
  configuration schema validator is not case-insensitive, so renaming them
  would have meant a settings migration to avoid resetting them all, for no
  gain outside the server
- The historical database migrations, which are a frozen record of what has
  already been applied; rewriting them risks breaking the migration pipeline.
  Nothing live refers to the dropped `MyListID` column

`fix` (`anidb`): **Keep MyList dates in the right timezone, and stop refetching the export**:

A code review over the branch turned up a set of faults, most of them one root
cause: AniDB works in UTC and the local database stores local time, and the two
were being compared and stored without converting between them.

**Parsed the HTTP export's view date as UTC** rather than parsing it as local
and shifting it, which moved a value that was already UTC by the server's
offset. The UDP parsers were already correct for the view date; their update
date now stays in UTC too, so it cannot land a day away from the export's.

**Converted at the two boundaries instead of at the call sites.** The local
watched date is read as UTC before being compared to what AniDB holds, and
`UserDataService` reads `LastPlayedAt` as local for both the change check and
the store. Doing only the store would have left the check comparing the two
kinds, so an unchanged date would have looked changed and saved on every sync.
Left as it was, every watched entry differed from AniDB forever, re-exported
itself on every sync, and wrote a view date off by the offset.

Also in this change:

- `MylistCache.ReplaceAll` returns the entries it stored. It carries forward
  the ED2K, size and generic-ness a fetch cannot rediscover, and the caller was
  getting its own list back without them — so the sync that triggered a fetch
  counted those entries as unclassified and re-added generic entries it
  already had
- A full export is fetched one at a time. The queue's concurrency groups
  already serialise each family of jobs against itself, but a sync and an
  entry job are in different ones, and a plugin calling in is in neither
- `NO_SUCH_EPISODE` is accepted when editing a generic entry, as the request
  it replaced did. Editing an entry for an episode AniDB no longer has failed
  the job instead of completing it
- Scheduling a sync with `Preview` set is refused. It resolved away silently,
  so a plugin asking for a preview got a real sync that wrote exactly what it
  asked not to
- Restored a shipped SQLite migration that the `Mylist` rename had edited

`fix`: **Remove missing files from the MyList when asked to, not when asked not to**:

`RemoveMissingFiles` passed its `removeMylist` flag straight into
`RemoveRecordWithOpenTransaction`'s `skipEvents` parameter. That parameter
covers the secondary events — outward side effects, the MyList removal among
them — so it is the inverse: asking to remove from the MyList skipped it, and
asking not to did it. The two actions a user picks between each did what the
other one's name says.

Passed `skipEvents: !removeMylist`, by name rather than by position.

**Collapsed the two actions into one.** `RemoveMissingFilesNoMylistSyncAction`
existed only to carry the other value of the flag, so it is now a
`RemoveMylist` parameter on `RemoveMissingFilesAction` instead, in the same
shape `DownloadAllImagesAction` already uses. It carries a `[Display]` name
ready for the action system to render it.

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Rename `VideoList` to `Videos` on `IEpisode` and `IMovie`**:

`ISeries` already exposed its files as `Videos`, while `IEpisode` and `IMovie`
called the same thing `VideoList`. They were the only two `*List`-suffixed
properties in the whole abstraction, so the suffix was an outlier rather than
a convention.

Added `Videos` to both and left `VideoList` behind as a default implementation
forwarding to it, marked obsolete. Consumers keep compiling and get a
deprecation warning; implementers now implement `Videos`.

Also in this change:

- Updated the five implementations and every caller. One in
  `VideoRelocationService` was invisible to the compiler behind a file-wide
  `CS0618` suppression that is there for something else

`refactor` (`anidb`): **Resolve the Mylist action scope through the abstractions**:

`MylistActionScope` cast `IShokoGroup`, `IShokoSeries` and `IShokoEpisode`
down to the concrete server models to reach their files. The casts bought
nothing: `ISeries.Videos` and `IEpisode.Videos` already expose them, and
everything the scope feeds — `ScheduleAddVideo`, `ScheduleDisposeVideo`,
`ScheduleSync` — takes `IVideo` anyway.

Dropped them, so the actions no longer reference `Shoko.Server.Models` at all.

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.83**.

`chore` (`anidb`): **Sort and prune the usings around Mylist**.

`feat` (`anidb`): **Make the Mylist sync plan a thing you can look at and hand back**:

A sync reported counts and nothing else, so there was no way to see what it was
about to change before it changed it, and no way to act on part of it.

**Added `MylistSyncPlan`** — what a sync worked out that it should do, and when
it worked it out — returned on `MylistSyncResult`. `MylistSyncOptions.PlanOnly`
works one out and returns it having done none of it: nothing local is written
and nothing is sent to AniDB, though the MyList is still fetched, since the
plan comes from it.

**A step carries what it acts on, not ids for them.** The video, both views of
the episode, and the MyList entry are on the step, along with the local watched
state — so a step holds both sides of the comparison that produced it, and can
be shown without looking anything up. `MemberNotNullWhen` predicates say which
combinations hold.

**Added `IMylistService.ApplySyncPlanAsync`** to carry a plan out. A plan need
not have come from a sync, so the whole of it is checked before any of it runs
and nothing runs at all if a step does not hold up — reported through
`GenericValidationException`, keyed by the step it came from. Past that point
the steps are independent, and one that fails unexpectedly is logged and
skipped rather than abandoning the rest.

Also in this change:

- Added the `AlreadyInDesiredState` kind, for a step the entry already
  satisfies. A healthy sync never plans one: it only reaches for a step once it
  has found a difference, so one appearing means the rules that decided to
  write and the check for whether writing is needed disagree — and the entry
  will be planned again on every sync until they stop
- `MylistSyncDirection` gained `None`, which is what that kind reads as, so a
  plan groups into three honest buckets without inspecting anything else
- A step's identity is checked against what it names: pairing a list id with
  the wrong file or episode would edit an entry the caller never asked about
- `CreatedAt` is informational. Nothing refuses a plan for being old, and an
  old one is safe to apply, since a step carries no values of its own

`feat` (`api`): **Add `AniDB/MyList/Sync/Plan` for looking at a sync before running it**:

There is no way to reach `IMylistService` from outside the server yet, so
planning a sync and applying part of it needed an APIv3 surface.

Five endpoints work out a plan — for everything, or confined to a group,
series, episode or file — and `Sync/Plan/Apply` carries one back out. The
scoped ones plan by episode rather than by file, so they cover an episode's
generic entry alongside the file entries of any files it has, and still work
for an episode with no files at all.

**Two models that overlap on purpose.** The output carries each step's file,
episode, local watched state and MyList entry, so a client can render a plan
without looking anything up. The input reads only the kind and one or two ids.
Its property names are a subset of the output's, and unknown properties are
ignored, so the body a plan endpoint returned can be posted straight back with
the unwanted steps removed. They are separate types so the generated client
offers only what apply actually reads.

**A caller chooses what to do, never what gets written.** No values cross the
wire: the watched date, storage state and delete type are all taken from
current state when a step runs. Changing a step's kind, or adding steps a sync
never proposed, is a thing an administrator may legitimately want; writing an
arbitrary date onto the user's MyList is not.

Also in this change:

- The controller forces the plan-only flag on rather than trusting the body, so
  no request to a planning endpoint can change anything
- Unresolvable ids are reported per step, since ids only exist at this layer;
  whether a step makes sense is left to the service, and its validation errors
  are passed through as-is
- A plan built here is stamped with the time it was built, rather than echoing
  whatever the caller sent

`chore`: **Sort usings**.

`fix` (`anidb`): **Break the dependency cycle through the Mylist service**:

`AnimeSeriesService` takes `IVideoReleaseService`, which took `IMylistService`,
which takes `AnimeSeriesService` — a closed loop that the container cannot
resolve. `UserDataService` already sidestepped its own edge of this with a
hand-rolled lazy field; the release service now does the same through
`Lazy<IMylistService>`, resolved by the existing `LazyResolver<>` registration.

Deferring construction is inert here: the service holds no construction side
effects beyond two semaphores, and it stays a singleton, so the sync and fetch
locks still guard every caller.

- Collapsed the two-line registration into `AddSingleton<IMylistService, MylistService>()`, as nothing resolves the concrete type
- Fixed the indentation of the `CheckAndAutoManage` call while in there

`chore` (`anidb`): **Spell MyList as two words in prose again**:

The one-word `Mylist` was only ever meant for identifiers, namespaces and
filenames. It had leaked into the places a person reads: log messages, action
and job display names, queue result keys, and the config section labels the
schema generator emits for the UI.

The `SectionName` labels are display-only — they land in `x-uiDefinition`, not
in the persisted config — so nothing here needs a settings migration.

- Left the `MyList_*` settings, the user data directory and the APIv3 route untouched, as they already used the two-word spelling

`fix` (`anidb`): **Convert local dates to UTC before sending them to AniDB**:

`GetAniDBDateAsSeconds` subtracted a UTC epoch with raw tick arithmetic, and
`DateTime.Kind` takes no part in that, so a local value reached AniDB as its own
wall clock. A watched date recorded at 17:13Z in UTC+2 was sent as 19:13Z and
has sat two hours ahead of itself ever since.

The old `CommandRequest_SyncMyList` fed it a value it had just converted the
other way, on read — a round trip with the conversion on one leg only — so
entries it touched are skewed by one local offset and stay that way until
something rewrites them.

`Unspecified` is deliberately left at face value rather than converted. The
callers passing one are sending a calendar date, not an instant: air dates
arrive as an unspecified midnight, and shifting one lands it on the day before
anywhere east of UTC.

- Added tests covering all three kinds; the two local ones fail against the old conversion under a non-UTC zone, while the air date and null cases hold either way

`test` (`queue`): **A job whose Title reads an injected service enqueues**: (_Skip CI_)

Pins the regression the previous commit fixed. TitleFromServiceJob is
shaped like ActionExecutionJob - its display members read an injected
service rather than its own properties - and enqueuing it threw before.
Checked by reverting the fix: the test fails, and passes again with it.
The harness now resolves jobs through ActivatorUtilities, which is what
the scheduler does.

`fix`: **Fix old api that was broken with nullable migration**.

`fix` (`config`): **Accept string enum values regardless of casing**:

The JSON schema validator compared enum values ordinally while both
`StringEnumConverter` and `JsonStringEnumConverter` match string enum
members case-insensitively, so a hand-written `"mysql"` threw a
`ConfigurationValidationException` on load even though the deserializer
would have parsed it to `DatabaseType.MySQL` without complaint.

- Matched enum values case-insensitively in `ValidateEnum`, preferring an
  exact match so a correctly cased value can never be claimed by a member
  that only differs in casing
- Added a `NormalizeEnum` hook, overridden in `ShokoJsonSchemaValidator`,
  that rewrites a loosely matched value to the casing the member is
  declared with, so the stored configuration is canonical again after the
  next save
- Set `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive` on the `System.Text.Json` options to
  match Newtonsoft, which silently fell back to the default value for a
  property whose name did not match exactly
- Moved the alias lookup into `ShokoJsonSchemaGenerator.TryResolveEnumAlias`
  next to the code that builds the list, fixing an environment variable
  override splitting `aliasValues` on `","` where it was joined with `", "`

`fix` (`queue`): **Build jobs through DI so display members can read services**:

Enqueue built the instance with GetUninitializedObject and then read
Title, Details and TypeName off it, so a job whose display members touch
an injected service threw NullReferenceException before anything was
persisted. ActionExecutionJob.Title does exactly that, which made every
action invocation a 500 with nothing queued to retry. Only public
read/write properties are serialised, so this does not change job data.

Added `ActionScope.Video`, mirroring the existing `Episode` scope end to

`fix` (`config`): **Send the visibility toggle's inverse condition**:

`VisibilityAttribute.InverseToggleCondition` was never emitted into
`x-uiDefinition`. The disable toggle beside it has always carried its
`inverseCondition`, and the WebUI reads both as non-optional
(`useVisibility.tsx:21` and `:40`), so a property whose visibility toggle
was declared inverted rendered as though it were not.

`feat` (`core`): **Resolve `Lazy<T>` from the container**:

Services caught in a dependency cycle broke it by injecting
`IServiceProvider`, holding a nullable backing field, and resolving on
first use with `??=`. That works but repeats at every site, hides the real
dependency from the constructor, and races — two threads can both resolve.

`LazyResolver<T>` is registered as an open generic, so any `Lazy<TService>`
is resolvable and a cyclic dependency can be declared in the constructor
like any other. `Lazy<T>` handles the thread-safety the `??=` did not.

`VideoReleaseService` is converted as the worked example; its
`IServiceProvider` existed only for this and is gone. `AnidbService` still
uses the old pattern in three places and can follow separately — it has a
long constructor and the change is mechanical but noisy.

Note this is only valid for singletons: the captured provider is whichever
resolved the consumer, so a scoped dependency pulled through a singleton
would outlive its scope. Equally true of the pattern it replaces; the
remarks say so.

`chore` (`api`): **Report the missing-password error on the password field**:

`AddModelError` named `Username` for "A new user must have a password
set.", so the message surfaced against the wrong field.

`fix` (`plugin`): **Drop a manifest already read from the same address**:

Keyed by package and source together, not by package alone. One package
appearing twice in a repository is meaningful - a stable manifest and a
dev manifest are the same package at two addresses, and the merge in
GetAvailablePackageManifests unions their releases on purpose. The same
package read twice from the same address is a repository listing an
entry twice, which duplicated every release it carried.

`fix` (`plugin`): **Verify declared dependencies at startup**:

`ScanForPlugins` parsed `PackageDependencies` and then nobody read them, so only
install and enable/disable enforced them. A Kahn pass over the winning entry per
id now ranks `LoadOrder` so dependencies register first, and clears `CanLoad` on
anything whose required dependency is absent, disabled, unloadable, out of range
or itself refused, cycles included. Both turn `internal set` (which drops
`required`) so a plugin cannot rewrite the verdict handed to it.

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Let only the core write plugin state**:

`IsEnabled` and `IsPinned` follow `CanLoad` and `LoadOrder` to `internal set`,
now that the core is the only friend assembly that can reach them. That takes
the hand-written backing field for `UninstalledAt` with it: the setter swallowed
a null and an overwrite to defend a field plugins can no longer touch, and the
one writer already re-checks `IsInstalled` under `lock (_pluginTypes)`.

`fix` (`api`): **Stop excluding unknown-air-date episodes from missing-episodes query**:

`GetMissing()` required `AirDate != 0`, silently dropping episodes with an
unknown air date even when the anime has already finished airing. This
disagreed with `AniDB_Episode.HasAired`, which treats an unknown air date
on a finished anime as aired. Loosened the SQL to a coarse pre-filter and
added the exact `HasAired` check in C#, matching `AnimeSeriesService.UpdateStats`.

`fix` (`core`): **Refresh anime stats after a release is saved**:

`SaveReleaseForVideo` never triggered a stats recalculation for the anime
a file was just linked to. `AnimeSeries.MissingEpisodeCount` (and other
cached stats) only refreshed via AniDB MyList sync, group-status refresh,
or a manual API call — never via the normal file-import pipeline. This let
the dashboard's missing-episode count go stale as soon as a previously
missing episode's file was imported, disagreeing with the live
`MissingEpisodes/Series` query. Enqueues `RefreshAnimeStatsJob` for each
affected anime after a release is saved, same job used by
`GetAniDBReleaseGroupStatusJob`.

`fix` (`api`): **Serialize AniDB status update type as a string**:

UpdateType in AniDBStatusUpdateSignalRModel was serialized as an
integer by SignalR because it lacked a string enum converter, unlike the
v3 API models. Added a StringEnumConverter attribute so the
udp.stateUpdate and http.stateUpdate events match the v3 convention.

`IVideoStream.MatrixCoefficients` and `IAudioStream.BitRateMode`.

- Dropped the `!` bridges in `VideoStream` and `AudioStream`, so the backing properties now implement the members directly
- Made the matching `MediaInfo` APIv3 response properties nullable; the emitted JSON is unchanged

`fix` (`db`): **Use the WebAOM provider ID for migrated `GroupAwareRenamer` scripts**:

The `GroupAwareRenamer` branch sits inside `if (providerInfo is null)` but read
`providerInfo.ID`, so migrating any legacy `RenameScript` with that renamer type
threw a `NullReferenceException`. The surrounding code already builds the
configuration from `webAomRenamer`, which is the intended provider.

`fix` (`buildtools`): **Guard `ExtractGetV5TypeName` against a missing argument list**:

`inv.ArgumentList?.Arguments.Count < 1` lifts to a `null < 1` comparison that
evaluates to `false`, so a null argument list skipped the `continue` and was
dereferenced on the next line. Replaced with a property pattern that fails to
match on null.

`fix` (`anidb`): **Stop adding nulls to the parsed staff and character lists**:

`ParseStaff` and `ParseCharacter` return null when the `id` attribute is not an
int, but `ParseStaffs` and `ParseCharacters` added the result unchecked, so a
null reached `AnimeCreator`. Both now skip nulls, matching `ParseTags`.

`UnescapeXml` also never recursed: it decoded the original argument on every
iteration instead of the previous result, so the second pass always equalled the
first and the loop returned after decoding exactly once. It now feeds each
round back in, which is what the surrounding comment describes.

`fix` (`plex`): **Return `BadRequest` for an unknown user in `SyncForUser`**:

`RepoFactory.JMMUser.GetByID` can miss, and the result was dereferenced before
the `BadRequest("Invalid User ID")` below could be reached, so an unknown user
ID produced a `NullReferenceException` instead. Also constrained `userID` to a
positive range.

`fix` (`api`): **Emit the value of a bool filter parameter instead of its type name**:

`IWithBoolParameter` called `ToString()` on the expression object rather than on
`Parameter`, so `/api/v3/Filter` reported a lowercased type name in place of
`true`/`false`. Every other case in the switch reads `Parameter`.

`fix` (`anidb`): **Avoid dereferencing a missing vote in `SyncAniDBVotesJob`**:

The guard above only skips when the vote is absent *and* the user has no rating,
so a user-rated series with no AniDB vote reached the `VoteType` read with a
null vote. A property pattern keeps the temporary-vote fallback without the
dereference.

Renamed the `Search/{*query}` handler to `LegacySearch` and marked it `[Obsolete]`, delegating to the new endpoint. Added a_new_ `Search` endpoint that takes `query` as a query parameter. The new endpoint supports controlling the sorting via `skipSort` and searches absolute paths when the `AbsolutePaths` include type is set.

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.78**.

`feat` (`buildtools`): **Add --tag, and stop dropping the revision**:

The version was truncated to three parts when read back off the
assembly, so a four-part dev version never reached the manifest and the
Dev-channel inference on it could never fire. The tag was inferred by a
describe that only matches `v*`, so a repo tagging `<name>-v1.2.3` got
`v1.2.3` recorded instead; --tag now overrides, inference is the
fallback, and the tag reaches the manifest entry rather than stopping
at the assembly stamp.
